message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on New York Avenue in this Monopoly auction.

I have $1,137 and own the orange set. New York Avenue would complete it. The current bid is $300. I have two active opponents.

I will not raise the bid above $300. I need cash to buy Virginia and Tennessee later, and to build houses. New York is already $100 over its list price. If I win it, I still need Tennessee to complete the orange set. Orange is the highest expected-value set in Monopoly. My opponent has no other orange properties, so New York would not immediately give them a monopoly.

None of the other players are close to an orange monopoly either. I am the only one who can complete it with New York Avenue. If someone else wins it, I would have to trade for it later at a high cost.

I will raise the bid to $350. That leaves $787 cash, which covers Virginia and Tennessee. I can still build three houses on the orange set later.

P2 is blocking my orange set. P3 is bidding aggressively. I am reconsidering whether to raise incrementally or jump. Incremental bids conserve cash if they drop out. A large jump might waste money. The property is overpriced at $300. It is not worth a non-monopoly holder.

I will bid $320 or $325 to stay in the auction without revealing my ceiling. I do not want to enter a bidding war that wastes cash on Virginia, Tennessee, and houses.

I will bid $325. I will drop if the bid exceeds $400.
